title: frequent `dns-forward-failing` error with warning in menubar icon (macOS, FreeBSD)
body:
### ⚠️ Last update 2025-12-06 I have a simplified repro and updated info in new issue https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/18146 --- I finally found a way to reliably reproduce this bug (see #18101) and created this simple POC: https://gist.github.com/reporter/6924d1f2d4ecedd11af62203ae8da37b Save, `chmod +x` and run the script. As long as you have `--accept-dns=false`, after ~15 seconds, you should get: --- - The information below is current as of Tailscale **1.92.0** rc running on macOS 26.1 (25B78) - The internal JIRA ticket is **TSS-68644** - I also experience this error on my pfSense router (FreeBSD) running Tailscale **1.90.6** so it is _NOT_ macOS-specific (N.B. that macOS _is_ loosely related to FreeBSD) - I'm tracking all of the `BUG-xxx` IDs in a separate [comment below](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/15389#issuecomment-2752998697) - I am happy to provide anything needed to help Tailscale debug this, including: direct access to the affected machine(s), remote access to a dedicated VM on my LAN that can reproduce this issue, any other logs or command output requested --- ### Bug Quite often (multiple times throughout the day, every day) I get the following warning: > **DNS Unavailable** > Tailscale can't reach the configured DNS servers. Internet connectivity may be affected. > > Code: dns-forward-failing
**⚠️N.B.** Despite this warning, **DNS resolution both inside and outside of my Tailnets works perfectly fine.** This occurs on both my MacBook Air M4 laptop (which often roams from network to network, WiFi to hotspot and various VPN connections) as well as on my Mac Mini M4 desktop. It NEVER self-corrects after entering this state. Running `tailscale down; sleep 5; tailscale up` does **_NOT_** resolve it. Only switching the main connection toggle to the OFF position and then back on clears it: After doing so, and without making any other configuration changes, Tailscale reports that all is well: ### Platform and Configuration - macOS 26.1 - Tailscale 1.91.150 (Standalone pkg version, but AppStore version is also affected) - "Use Tailscale DNS settings" **NOT** checked - I use a combination of a custom resolver file at `/etc/resolver/` directing `ts.net` queries to quad-100 as well as some statically defined entries in `/etc/hosts` for DNS resolution inside my tailnet Here's a screenshot of my Tailscale settings: Here is some output from `scutil --dns` in case it's relevant: ``` $ scutil --dns DNS configuration resolver #1 search domain[0] : lan search domain[1] : internal nameserver[0] comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Been working all day on trying to get more info on this problem. ### 1. Finding the code that triggers this error I dug through the code to find the area that sets this `dns-forward-failing` (dnsForwarderFailing) error condition. There are 3 places, all in [`net/dns/resolver/forwarder.go`](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/main/net/dns/resolver/forwarder.go): https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/92a114c66d296704d48045ee12c0fe28bb7f5b6c/net/dns/resolver/forwarder.go#L951-L955 https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/92a114c66d296704d48045ee12c0fe28bb7f5b6c/net/dns/resolver/forwarder.go#L1047-L1054 https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/92a114c66d296704d48045ee12c0fe28bb7f5b6c/net/dns/resolver/forwarder.go#L1071-L1079 The conditions to hit these codepaths appear to be 1. No DNS resolvers present at all 2. None of the configured resolvers are returning valid responses 3. Timeout (no valid OR error response at all from any resolvers)? Not sure which case (cases?) I'm hitting, but I'm starting to collect better debug info (read on) ### 2. Getting daemon health via CLI I found a way to check for Tailscale daemon health via the Terminal. ```bash TAILSCALE_BE_CLI=1 /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale status --json | jq .Health ``` Or, a bit nicer: ```bash TAILSCALE_BE_CLI=1 /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale status --json \ | jq -r '.Health | if length == 0 then "healthy" else "\(.[0])\n" | halt_error(1) end' ``` I've now wired up a daemon to check every 10 minutes for the issue and dump diagnostic output if/when it occurs. Hopefully this will lead to a solution. ### 3. "derp-1 does not know about peer" As I was looking at my daemon logs for clues, and noticed an unusual amount of logspam about a specific peer: `5DokL`: ``` # tailscale debug daemon-logs magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route (continues forever...) ``` Not sure if this is important (I think "no"). Can't find any documented way to map that **5DokL** to a specific peer–it's not in the UI or JSON output of any command I can find. I _did_ figure out that it is my laptop though, by poring over the macOS ULS logs ``` $ log show --last 10m --predicate 'composedMessage contains "5DokL"' 2025-07-06 17:33:36.473077-0400 0x82f01d Default 0x0 22402 0 IPNExtension: magicsock: derp-1 does not know about peer [5DokL], removing route 2025-07-06 17:33:40.227246-0400 0x82f047 Default 0x0 22402 0 IPNExtension: open-conn-track: timeout opening (TCP 100.114.101.103:22000 => 100.84.155.68:22000) to node [5DokL]; online=no, lastseen=recent, lastRecv=5m55s ``` **22000** is my Syncthing port so I figure this is just syncthing constantly trying to connect to my sleeping laptop, and Tailscale reporting that it isn't online. **The logspam stops when I wake my laptop up from sleep.** > Related "derp-N does not know about peer" issues: https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/14623 and https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/11565 ### 4. "No Search Domains Found" `tailscale dns status` always says `no search domains found` even when my machine clearly has them: Is Tailscale referring to the global search domains here, or the _scoped_ ones for its `utun` interface? Because I do see that there aren't any applied there... maybe that's why?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
The automation is working well. I wired it up to automatically bounce Tailscale when this condition is detected. It's also generating nice logs and debug info every time this occurs, which is multiple times throughout the day.

As of now, here's what the script collects every time an unhealthy state is detected:

- BUG ID (`tailscale bugreport`)
- Status (`tailscale status --json`)
- DNS status (`tailscale dns status --all`)
- Netcheck (`tailscale netcheck --verbose --format json`)
- Ping to an _online_ peer, that's not self (`tailscale ping w.x.y.z`)
- Dump from [`dns-osconfig`](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/f1c7b463cd1cbc6de634a8b75a14cfeca498756f/ipn/localapi/localapi.go#L2543) (`serveDNSOSConfig`) via local API
- DNS query for `tailscale.com` to every server listed in the `Nameserver[]` JSON object from the `dns-osconfig` above
- DNS query for random tailnet peer using Quad100 (`tailscale dns query <peer_hostname>`)
- Output from each of the following `scutil` commands:
    - `scutil --dns`
    - `scutil --nwi`
    - `scutil --nc list`
    - `scutil --nc status Tailscale`
    - `scutil --nc show Tailscale`
- Full macOS .logarchive (`log collect --last 10m`) from the last 10 minutes (healthcheck runs every 10 minutes, so theoretically there should be something in the logs to indicate what caused the current failure)

All of these are saved in a timestamped folder. So far I've collected 8 "unhealthy" and 8 "healthy" reports. @participant6 Anything useful I can do with these, or additional info to collect at the time of the issue?

Let me know if I can provide these logs to someone to help track this down?
